description: Blocks in the Simulink > Sinks library and the closely related visualization blocks and tools that consume signals rather than produce them: scopes and numeric displays for watching a run, To Workspace, To File and Record for logging data, Outport and Out Bus Element for passing signals out of a subsystem or model, and Terminator and Stop Simulation for housekeeping. Parameter names given here are the programmatic ones accepted by set_param.

tools.name: Scope
tools.description: Displays one or more signals against simulation time in a scope window, with cursors, triggers, measurements and up to 96 input ports arranged over a grid of displays. It is the default way to look at a signal while developing a model, and it can also log the displayed data to the workspace. Scope windows are separate from the model diagram, so their settings live in a configuration object rather than a plain dialog.
tools.usage: Simulink > Sinks > Scope (also Simulink > Commonly Used Blocks)

parameters.name: NumInputPorts
parameters.description: Number of input ports, 1 to 96. Each port can be routed to a different display.

parameters.name: OpenAtSimulationStart
parameters.description: 'on' opens the scope window automatically when the simulation starts.

parameters.name: LayoutDimensions
parameters.description: [rows cols] grid of displays inside the scope window.

parameters.name: TimeSpan
parameters.description: Length of the visible x-axis in seconds, or 'Auto' to follow the model stop time.

parameters.name: YLimits
parameters.description: Two-element [min max] vector setting the y-axis range of the active display.

parameters.name: DataLogging
parameters.description: 'on' saves the displayed data to the MATLAB workspace at the end of the run.

parameters.name: DataLoggingVariableName
parameters.description: Name of the workspace variable the logged scope data is written to.

parameters.name: SampleTime
parameters.description: Interval at which the scope samples its inputs; '-1' inherits.

tools.notes: Most display settings must be written through the ScopeConfiguration object returned by get_param, not with set_param on the block. In headless or CI runs set OpenAtSimulationStart to false, or replace Scope blocks with To Workspace using replace_block, to avoid opening figures.

tools.name: Floating Scope
tools.description: A scope with no input ports: instead of being wired to a signal, it displays whichever signals you select in the Signal Selector. That means you can probe different parts of a model without adding or deleting lines, which keeps a large diagram readable during debugging. Apart from the connection mechanism it has the same displays, cursors and measurements as the Scope block.

parameters.name: OpenAtSimulationStart
parameters.description: 'on' opens the scope window when the simulation starts.

parameters.name: LayoutDimensions
parameters.description: [rows cols] grid of displays inside the window.

parameters.name: YLimits
parameters.description: [min max] y-axis range of the active display.

parameters.name: ShowLegend
parameters.description: 'on' shows the signal legend, which matters when several selected signals share one display.

parameters.name: ShowGrid
parameters.description: 'on' draws grid lines.

parameters.name: AxesScaling
parameters.description: How the axes rescale: 'Manual', 'Auto', 'Updates'.

tools.notes: The data logging, sample time, time span and save format parameters of the ordinary Scope do not apply to floating scopes. Signals selected in a floating scope must be visible at the level being probed; signals inside a referenced model need logging turned on to be selectable.

tools.name: Scope Viewer
tools.description: A scope attached to a signal as a viewer rather than as a block, so nothing is added to the diagram at all — the signal simply gains a viewer badge. Because viewers are model-level annotations, they can be added and removed without dirtying the structure of the model, which makes them the least intrusive way to watch signals in a model under configuration control. Functionally the display is the same as a Floating Scope.
tools.usage: Select a signal, then Simulation tab > Prepare > Add Viewer > Scope

parameters.name: Add Viewer
parameters.description: Simulation tab, Prepare section — attaches a viewer of the chosen type to the currently selected signal.

parameters.name: Signal Selector
parameters.description: Toolbar button inside the viewer window used to add or remove the signals it displays.

parameters.name: Viewers and Generators Manager
parameters.description: Dialog listing every viewer and signal generator attached to the model, where they can be edited or deleted.

tools.example:
1. Open the model and click the signal you want to watch.
2. On the Simulation tab, in the Prepare section, click Add Viewer and choose Scope.
3. Run the simulation; the viewer window opens showing that signal.
4. Use the Signal Selector in the viewer toolbar to add further signals.
% Programmatic alternative: place a Floating Scope block instead
% add_block('simulink/Sinks/Floating Scope', 'mdl/Probe');
tools.notes: Unlike the Floating Scope there is no library block to add with add_block — viewers are created through the Add Viewer workflow. Viewers are ignored during code generation and in Rapid Accelerator mode, so a run that must log data needs To Workspace, Record or signal logging instead.

tools.name: Display
tools.description: Shows the numeric value of its input directly on the block icon in the model canvas, updating as the simulation runs. It is the quickest way to read a scalar or small vector at a glance without opening a scope window. Format and update rate are configurable, and it can be made floating so it has no input port and shows whichever signal you select.

parameters.name: Format
parameters.description: Numeric display format: 'short' (default), 'long', 'short_e', 'long_e', 'bank', 'hex', 'binary', 'decimal', 'octal'.

parameters.name: Decimation
parameters.description: Show the value at every n-th sample. Default '1'.

parameters.name: Floating
parameters.description: 'on' removes the input port so the block displays a signal selected in the Signal Selector instead. Default 'off'.

parameters.name: SampleTime
parameters.description: Rate at which the block samples its input; '-1' inherits.

tools.notes: The block shows at most about 200 vector elements or a 20-by-10 matrix, with a small black triangle marking omitted values — resize the block to see more. It displays but does not store anything; use To Workspace or Record when the value has to survive the run.

tools.name: Record
tools.description: The modern combined logging and visualization sink: it plots its inputs, logs them to the workspace, to a MAT-file, to a Parquet file, or to any combination of those, from a single block with up to many input ports. It replaces the need to place a Scope next to a To Workspace next to a To File, and it integrates with the Simulation Data Inspector for inspecting the result. Use it as the default data-capture block in new models.

parameters.name: NumPorts
parameters.description: Number of input ports on the block.

parameters.name: RecordToWorkspace
parameters.description: 'on' logs the recorded data to a MATLAB workspace variable.

parameters.name: VariableName
parameters.description: Name of the workspace variable written when RecordToWorkspace is on.

parameters.name: RecordToFile
parameters.description: 'on' writes the recorded data to a file.

parameters.name: FileName
parameters.description: Name and location of the output file (.mat or .parquet).

parameters.name: Decimation
parameters.description: Record every n-th sample.

parameters.name: MaxDataPoints
parameters.description: Limit the record to the last N data points; 'inf' keeps everything.

parameters.name: FrameSettings
parameters.description: Input processing mode for frame-based versus sample-based inputs.

parameters.name: ParquetCompression
parameters.description: Compression used when writing Parquet output.

tools.notes: Parquet output is the option to reach for with very long runs, since it streams to disk and compresses. The XY Graph block is an alternative configuration of this same block. Data recorded to a MAT-file can be replayed directly with the From File source block.

tools.name: To Workspace
tools.description: Writes its input signal into a variable in the MATLAB workspace at the end of the simulation, or into the SimulationOutput object returned by sim. It is the standard bridge from a Simulink run to MATLAB post-processing, plotting and assertions in a test script. The save format controls whether you get a timeseries, a structure with time, or a bare array.

parameters.name: VariableName
parameters.description: Name of the variable created. Default 'simout'.

parameters.name: SaveFormat
parameters.description: 'Timeseries' (default), 'Structure With Time', 'Structure' or 'Array'.

parameters.name: MaxDataPoints
parameters.description: Keep only the last N points; 'inf' (default) keeps them all.

parameters.name: Decimation
parameters.description: Record every n-th sample. Default '1'.

parameters.name: SampleTime
parameters.description: Sampling interval for the logged data; '-1' (default) inherits from the input.

parameters.name: Save2DSignal
parameters.description: How matrix signals are stacked: '3-D array (concatenate along third dimension)' or '2-D array (concatenate along first dimension)'.

parameters.name: FixptAsFi
parameters.description: 'on' (default) logs fixed-point data as a fi object rather than converting it to double.

tools.notes: With the Single simulation output option enabled (the default for new models) the variable appears as a field of the Simulink.SimulationOutput returned by sim rather than in the base workspace. An unbounded MaxDataPoints on a long fine-step run can exhaust memory — decimate or use To File / Record instead.

tools.name: To File
tools.description: Streams its input signal into a MAT-file incrementally as the simulation runs, rather than accumulating it in memory. That makes it the right sink for very long runs and high-rate signals where To Workspace would run out of memory. The resulting file is directly readable by the From File source block, which makes record-and-replay workflows straightforward.

parameters.name: FileName
parameters.description: Name or path of the MAT-file to write. Default 'untitled.mat'.

parameters.name: MatrixName
parameters.description: Name of the variable stored inside the MAT-file. Default 'ans'.

parameters.name: SaveFormat
parameters.description: 'Timeseries' (default) or 'Array'.

parameters.name: Decimation
parameters.description: Write every n-th sample. Default '1'.

parameters.name: SampleTime
parameters.description: Sampling interval of the written data; '-1' (default) inherits.

tools.notes: The file is overwritten at the start of every simulation, so a sweep needs a distinct FileName per run, which a Simulink.SimulationInput setBlockParameter call can supply. The Record block is the newer alternative and additionally supports Parquet output and simultaneous workspace logging.

tools.name: XY Graph
tools.description: Plots one input against another on an X-Y plot instead of against time: the first input supplies the x coordinate and the second the y coordinate. This is the view you need for phase-plane portraits, limit cycles, hysteresis loops and any two-state trajectory where the shape of the orbit matters more than its timing. In current releases it is a configuration of the Record block, so it also logs the data it plots.

parameters.name: Port 1 (x)
parameters.description: First input port; supplies the horizontal coordinate of each plotted point.

parameters.name: Port 2 (y)
parameters.description: Second input port; supplies the vertical coordinate.

parameters.name: RecordToWorkspace
parameters.description: 'on' also logs the plotted data to a workspace variable (inherited from the Record block configuration).

parameters.name: VariableName
parameters.description: Name of that workspace variable.

parameters.name: Decimation
parameters.description: Plot and record every n-th sample.

tools.notes: The older MATLAB-figure-based XY Graph is documented as not recommended; the block in the current Sinks library is the Record-based version, so it accepts Record's programmatic parameters rather than the legacy xmin/xmax/ymin/ymax fields. Double-click the block, or right-click and choose Open in New Window, to see the plot.

tools.name: Outport
tools.description: Creates an output port: at the top level of a model it exports a signal to the caller (into the yout field of the SimulationOutput, or to the parent when the model is referenced), and inside a subsystem it defines one of the subsystem block's output ports. Ports are numbered sequentially and renumber automatically when one is deleted. For conditionally executed subsystems it also defines what the output holds while the subsystem is disabled.
tools.usage: Simulink > Sinks > Outport (also Simulink > Ports & Subsystems and Commonly Used Blocks)

parameters.name: Port
parameters.description: Port number, which sets the position of the port on the parent subsystem block.

parameters.name: OutDataTypeStr
parameters.description: Output data type, including 'Inherit: auto', built-in types, 'Bus: <object>' and enumerations.

parameters.name: PortDimensions
parameters.description: Required signal dimensions: '-1' (inherited), an integer, or [rows cols].

parameters.name: InitialOutput
parameters.description: Value held before the first execution of a conditionally executed subsystem.

parameters.name: OutputWhenDisabled
parameters.description: 'held' or 'reset' — what an enabled subsystem's output does while it is disabled.

parameters.name: SampleTime
parameters.description: Sample time of the port; '-1' inherits.

parameters.name: SignalName
parameters.description: Name given to the signal leaving the port, which is also the name used in logged output.

tools.notes: The library block is named Out1, so the add_block source path is 'simulink/Sinks/Out1' even though the block reference page is titled Outport. Deleting an Outport renumbers the remaining ports, which silently rewires the parent subsystem — check port numbers after programmatic deletion.

tools.name: Out Bus Element
tools.description: Publishes one element of a bus out through a named external port, without needing an explicit Bus Creator plus Outport pair. Several Out Bus Element blocks that share a port name combine into a single bus on that port, so a subsystem's interface can be built up element by element next to the signals that produce them. This keeps wide interfaces readable and avoids long bundles of lines crossing the diagram.
tools.usage: Simulink > Sinks > Out Bus Element (also Simulink > Ports & Subsystems)

parameters.name: PortName
parameters.description: Name of the external output port this block contributes to. Blocks sharing a name share a port.

parameters.name: Element
parameters.description: Name of the bus element this block writes, e.g. 'sensors.speed'.

parameters.name: Port
parameters.description: Position of the port on the parent subsystem block.

parameters.name: OutDataTypeStr
parameters.description: Data type of the element, including inheritance options.

parameters.name: SampleTime
parameters.description: Sample time of the element; '-1' inherits.

tools.notes: Port names must be unique within a system and each element may be written by only one block, otherwise the writes overlap and Simulink errors. In Bus Element is the matching source-side block; Bus Creator plus Outport remains the equivalent classic construction.

tools.name: Terminator
tools.description: Caps an output port whose signal is deliberately unused, so that Simulink does not warn about an unconnected port. Library blocks and subsystems often produce diagnostics or secondary outputs that a given model does not need, and terminating them keeps the diagnostic viewer clean and makes the intent explicit to a reader. The block accepts any data type, dimension and complexity.
tools.usage: Simulink > Sinks > Terminator (also Simulink > Commonly Used Blocks)
tools.notes: Ground is the mirror-image block for unconnected input ports. Terminator does not support variable-size signals. Because it discards data, never use it on a signal you later expect to find in the logs.

tools.name: Stop Simulation
tools.description: Ends the simulation as soon as its input becomes nonzero, completing the current time step first. Drive it from a Relational Operator or a fault-detection expression to stop a run when a variable leaves its valid range, when a controller converges, or when a test objective is met, instead of always running to the configured stop time. Any nonzero element of a vector input triggers the stop.

parameters.name: Port_1
parameters.description: Scalar, vector or matrix input of type double or boolean. The simulation stops when any element is nonzero.

tools.notes: It can only stop a simulation, never pause one — use set_param(mdl,'SimulationCommand','pause') for that. Inside a For Iterator subsystem the stop takes effect only after all iterations of that time step finish. The actual stop time then differs from the configured StopTime, so read it from the SimulationOutput metadata rather than assuming.

tools.name: Dashboard Scope
tools.description: A scope that lives on the model canvas itself and connects to signals by binding rather than by signal lines, so it can be dropped anywhere in the diagram without rerouting anything. Combined with the other dashboard controls and indicators it turns a model into an interactive panel you can watch and tune while the simulation runs. It traces up to eight signals from an array or bus and supports any Simulink data type including enumerations.

parameters.name: Binding
parameters.description: Cell array of Simulink.HMI.SignalSpecification objects naming the signals the scope traces.

parameters.name: TimeSpan
parameters.description: Length of the visible time window: 'auto' or a scalar number of seconds.

parameters.name: UpdateMode
parameters.description: 'Wrap' or 'Scroll' — how the display advances once the time span is filled.

parameters.name: YLimits
parameters.description: [min max] vector fixing the y-axis range.

parameters.name: NormalizeYAxis
parameters.description: 'on' normalizes traces so signals of very different magnitude are comparable.

parameters.name: Colors
parameters.description: Struct array with Auto, Color and LineStyle fields controlling each trace's appearance.

parameters.name: LegendPosition
parameters.description: 'Top', 'Right', 'InsideTop', 'InsideRight' or 'Hide'.

parameters.name: Grid
parameters.description: 'All', 'Horizontal', 'Vertical' or 'None'.

tools.notes: Dashboard blocks have no ports; they attach through the Binding parameter or interactively in connect mode. They are ignored by code generation and are not supported in Rapid Accelerator mode, so they are a tuning and demonstration aid rather than a logging mechanism.

tools.name: TimeScopeConfiguration
tools.description: The configuration object behind every Scope, Floating Scope and Time Scope block, obtained with get_param(block,'ScopeConfiguration'). Almost all scope appearance and behaviour — layout, axis limits, legends, time span, data logging — is set through this object's properties with dot notation rather than through set_param on the block. It is therefore the key to configuring scopes from a build script or a test harness.

parameters.name: NumInputPorts
parameters.description: Number of scope input ports, 1 to 96.

parameters.name: LayoutDimensions
parameters.description: [rows cols] arrangement of displays within the scope window.

parameters.name: OpenAtSimulationStart
parameters.description: Logical; whether the scope window opens automatically when the run starts.

parameters.name: TimeSpan / TimeUnits / TimeDisplayOffset
parameters.description: Extent, units and origin of the x-axis.

parameters.name: YLimits / YLabel / AxesScaling
parameters.description: Y-axis range, label and autoscaling behaviour ('Manual', 'Auto', 'OnceAtStop', 'Updates').

parameters.name: ShowLegend / ShowGrid / Title
parameters.description: Annotation of the active display.

parameters.name: DataLogging / DataLoggingVariableName / DataLoggingSaveFormat
parameters.description: Whether and how the displayed data is saved to the workspace.

parameters.name: ActiveDisplay
parameters.description: Which display in the layout the display-specific properties above currently apply to.

tools.notes: Display-specific properties such as YLimits, Title and YLabel apply to whichever display ActiveDisplay currently points at, so set ActiveDisplay first when the layout has more than one. The Spectrum Analyzer block uses the analogous SpectrumAnalyzerBlockConfiguration object, retrieved the same way.

tools.name: Time Scope
tools.description: The DSP System Toolbox time-domain scope, which displays continuous, discrete, fixed-size, variable-size, floating-point, fixed-point and N-dimensional signals and adds signal statistics, peak finding, bilevel timing measurements and triggering. Use it instead of the base Scope when you need those measurements or frame-based multichannel display. It can also log the displayed signal data back to MATLAB.
tools.usage: DSP System Toolbox > Sinks > Time Scope

parameters.name: NumInputPorts
parameters.description: Number of input ports, 1 to 96.

parameters.name: OpenAtSimulationStart
parameters.description: 'on' opens the scope window when the simulation starts.

parameters.name: LayoutDimensions
parameters.description: [rows cols] grid of displays.

parameters.name: FrameBasedProcessing
parameters.description: Whether each input column is treated as a frame of one channel or as one sample of several channels.

parameters.name: SampleTime
parameters.description: Interval at which the scope updates; '-1' inherits.

parameters.name: DataLogging
parameters.description: 'on' saves the displayed data to the workspace.

parameters.name: DataLoggingVariableName
parameters.description: Workspace variable name for the logged data.

tools.notes: Requires DSP System Toolbox. Like the Simulink Scope it is configured through a TimeScopeConfiguration object rather than set_param. The MATLAB-side equivalent for use outside a model is the timescope System object, which also ships with Navigation Toolbox and Sensor Fusion and Tracking Toolbox.

tools.name: Spectrum Analyzer
tools.description: Displays the frequency spectrum of a time-domain signal, or plots a signal that is already in the frequency domain, with power, power-density and RMS views plus a spectrogram. It provides peak, channel, distortion, harmonic and cursor measurements, which makes it the tool of choice for checking filter responses, noise floors, THD and spurious content during a simulation. Averaging and the spectral estimation method are configurable.
tools.usage: DSP System Toolbox > Sinks > Spectrum Analyzer

parameters.name: InputDomain
parameters.description: 'Time' to estimate the spectrum of a time-domain input, or 'Frequency' to plot frequency-domain data directly.

parameters.name: SpectrumType
parameters.description: 'Power', 'Power density' or 'RMS'.

parameters.name: Method
parameters.description: Spectral estimation method: 'Filter bank' or 'Welch'.

parameters.name: SampleRate / SampleRateSource
parameters.description: Input sample rate, either inherited from the signal or specified as a property.

parameters.name: PlotAsTwoSidedSpectrum
parameters.description: true for a two-sided spectrum, false for one-sided.

parameters.name: FrequencyOffset
parameters.description: Offset applied to the frequency axis, for displaying a band around a carrier.

parameters.name: AveragingMethod
parameters.description: How successive spectra are smoothed, e.g. running or exponential averaging.

parameters.name: ViewType
parameters.description: 'Spectrum', 'Spectrogram' or both.

tools.notes: Requires DSP System Toolbox (it also ships in the Audio Toolbox Sinks library). Settings are written through the SpectrumAnalyzerBlockConfiguration object returned by get_param(blk,'ScopeConfiguration'). The spectrumAnalyzer System object is the MATLAB-side equivalent for use outside a model.

tools.name: Array Plot
tools.description: Plots the elements of a vector or array against their index rather than against simulation time, refreshing on every sample hit. This is the view you want for filter coefficients, FFT magnitude bins, histograms, spatial profiles and any quantity whose meaningful axis is position in the array. Stem, line, stair and bar plot styles and logarithmic axes are available.
tools.usage: DSP System Toolbox > Sinks > Array Plot

parameters.name: PlotType
parameters.description: 'Stem', 'Line', 'Stairs' or 'Bar'.

parameters.name: XDataMode
parameters.description: How the x-axis values are derived: from a sample increment and offset, or from custom data.

parameters.name: SampleIncrement / XOffset
parameters.description: Spacing and starting value of the x-axis when it is generated rather than supplied.

parameters.name: CustomXData
parameters.description: Explicit vector of x-axis values.

parameters.name: XScale / YScale
parameters.description: 'Linear' or 'Log' scaling of each axis.

parameters.name: ChannelNames
parameters.description: Names shown in the legend for each input channel.

parameters.name: LayoutDimensions
parameters.description: [rows cols] grid of displays.

parameters.name: OpenAtSimulationStart
parameters.description: Whether the window opens when the simulation starts.

tools.notes: Requires DSP System Toolbox. Accepts up to 96 input ports and supports double, single, fixed-point and complex data. dsp.ArrayPlot is the equivalent System object for plotting arrays from MATLAB code.

tools.name: Simulation Data Inspector
tools.description: The interactive viewer that collects every logged signal from a simulation into named runs, so that signals from different runs can be plotted together, compared with tolerances, inspected with cursors and exported. It is the place logged data goes when signal logging, Record blocks or scope logging are enabled, and it is the standard way to do a regression comparison between a baseline run and a new one. It is opened from the Simulation tab or from MATLAB.
tools.usage: Simulation tab > Review Results > Data Inspector, or Simulink.sdi.view from MATLAB

parameters.name: Simulink.sdi.view
parameters.description: Opens the Simulation Data Inspector; an optional argument selects the Inspect or Compare pane.

parameters.name: Simulink.sdi.clear
parameters.description: Clears all runs and signals currently held by the Inspector — use it at the start of a scripted test so old runs cannot be mistaken for new ones.

parameters.name: Simulink.sdi.close
parameters.description: Closes the Inspector, optionally saving the session to an MLDATX file first.

parameters.name: Simulink.sdi.setSubPlotLayout
parameters.description: Sets the grid of subplots in the Inspect pane.

parameters.name: Simulink.sdi.setNumCursors / Simulink.sdi.getCursorPositions
parameters.description: Add measurement cursors to the plots and read back where they sit.

parameters.name: Simulink.sdi.Run.create
parameters.description: Creates a run from workspace data so that measured or reference data can be compared against simulation output.

tools.notes: Signals only reach the Inspector if something logs them: mark signals for logging in the model, enable scope data logging, or use Record or To Workspace blocks. The Inspector keeps runs across MATLAB sessions in its archive, so clear it in automated tests to keep results deterministic.
